message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that uses an **RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **Note**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * The RTX A6000 GPU is available in the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` family.  
> * You must have the Compute Engine API enabled, a project set, and the `gcloud` CLI installed (or you can use the REST API directly).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

### Explanation

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script to run at boot. |

> **Tip**: If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` values accordingly.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

```json
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to call it

1. **Authenticate**: Use OAuth 2.0 to obtain an access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.
2. **Send the request**:  
   ```bash
   curl -X POST \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @instance.json \
     "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
   ```

Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] Compute Engine API enabled in your GCP project.  
- [ ] Billing enabled.  
- [ ] Enough quota for the selected machine type and GPU.  
- [ ] `gcloud` CLI authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
- [ ] (Optional) A startup script to install NVIDIA drivers or other packages.

Once the instance is created, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --project=${PROJECT_ID} --zone=${ZONE}
```

Enjoy your RTX A6000 GPU on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS!
